items.item: (2) The edge record's premises_of_the_ethics and the boundary model
items.how: one-root-to-its-edge. The condition's basis now says the condition says whose losses count and by itself ranks nothing. It says the ranking results take it held de se, and that on the reading that what has significance from a standpoint is what lies within its center's reach along a relation it is then the root's 续无外 (ownClosure_unrestricted_iff_noOutside). The F5 sentence is unchanged. The C item's name is now 'C, the requirement that an order rank each course above every course it widens, where a theorem takes it; where the condition holds de se, self-concern does what it asks, one way, between level paths whose admissions end' (zh in step), replacing 'an order ranking each course above every course it widens (C)'. The name carries self-concern because the page prints the name and not the basis. The basis now says: 'in the proofs a hypothesis, and that a life forms such an order is not shown'; the ranking on a finite listing and, one way, between level paths whose admitted (step, formation) pairs fit in a finite list, 'so that their admissions end'; 'for courses that go on forming without end it is not shown'; 'ranking by widening adds no premise beside the life's own concern: that concern already does it'; and widening as what every additive weighting counting each listed item above zero ranks higher. The premise declarations (Becoming.Unrestricted, Becoming.Comparison), their not-entailed theorems and their reviews are unchanged, so Q1 and the review-naming rule still hold. boundary.py gains PREMISE_LABELS = {'scope': 'Whose losses count', 'order': 'How courses are ranked'}. registry.py prints '**Hypotheses the ranking results take**, each only where a theorem takes it:', then '- **Whose losses count:** <name>, `<premise>`; ...' and '- **How courses are ranked:** ...', in place of '**For scope**' and '**For order**'. The keys stay 'scope'/'order' and 'premises_of_the_ethics': the generated shared-laws.json, boundary.field_findings' schema messages, registry.boundary_matching/boundary_status and test_boundary's fixtures all carry them, so renaming would break data the render writes. test_boundary's two page pins were re-pinned, with assertNotIn for '**For scope**' and '**For order**'. A new repository test holds the edge record's premises free of 'no second premise', 'courses that end', 'every positive weighting', 'argued, not shown', 'fixes scope' and 'an order ranking each course', and holds that the order item names the requirement and self-concern and its basis says additive.
